languageMotionQuote: Gentle and natural. Soft scroll-reveals, a slow settle on images, a small lift on cards. Nothing mechanical or fast. Durations: fast 180ms, base 360ms, slow 640ms. Easing: cubic-bezier(0.25, 0.8, 0.35, 1). Quick to leave, slow to arrive, no bounce at the end. Reveal: mask-grow. Arched images reveal by their rounded-top mask growing from 92% to full height while the image fades; text does a plain 10px fade-up alongside. Stagger: 90ms, capped at 6. Signature motion move: arch-open, used once per section on the lead image, so the page reads as doors opening onto daylight. Continuous motion: one is permitted (a slow hero crossfade of two genuine photos of the same space); never a marquee, never parallax.
languageMobileQuote: Daylight and abundance have to survive at 390px. The arch keeps its proportion on a phone rather than flattening. Type scale: display 2.75rem to 1.875rem, headings 1.75rem to 1.375rem, body 17px. Section rhythm py-16 md:py-24 lg:py-28. Do not drop the visible reviewed date on the seasonal list. Mobile-native affordance: long honest lists stay long.

tokens.derivation: Every figure is the language's own stated value, not an adaptation: 180/360/640ms, the 0.25/0.8/0.35/1 curve, 90ms stagger capped at 6, and the 10px text travel from the reveal spec (the template's neutral 16px was replaced, because the language asks for a plain 10px fade-up). Ledger anti-drift check: nj-electrical shipped 120/220/420 on 0.4/0/0.2/1 and mojo-steel 200/450/850 on 0.2/0.6/0.2/1; this build shares no duration and no curve with either.
tokens.location: web/src/styles/tokens.css :root, exposed to Tailwind via the @theme block; components bind with duration-(--motion-*) and ease-brand, never a literal

entrance.effect: enter-rise cascade at 90ms steps (eyebrow, h1, subheading, buttons), full sequence 640ms + 3x90ms = 910ms to the last element, primary CTA lands at 180ms delay, inside the 500ms budget. On the two arched heroes (Home, How it works) the lead image runs arch-open as a pure CSS load entrance (@keyframes arch-open), no observer.

reveal.variant: mask-grow for the one lead arched image per section (.arch-reveal: clip-path inset 8%-to-0 with the arch radius while opacity settles 0.35-to-1); every other element does the language's plain 10px fade-up via .reveal

interaction.hover: Buttons lift -0.5px translate plus fill deepen (accent to accent-strong, primary to primary-light); text links underline-wipe with colour shift; strip rows tint to surface; FAQ summaries tint to primary-soft. Never colour alone.
interaction.focusVisible: Global 2px accent-strong outline with 2px offset on a, button, summary, input, select, textarea (global.css).
interaction.active: Buttons and the call bar translate back down 1px on press (the touch confirmation), timed at --motion-fast.

transitionNames: page-heading (the h1 in every hero variant, so headings morph between routes rather than cross-fading)
persist: Header (transition:persist), so the nav and call affordance do not blink between pages

signatureMotion.name: arch-open
signatureMotion.what: The rounded-top mask of a section's lead arched image grows from 92% to full height over the slow duration while the image settles from 0.35 to full opacity.
signatureMotion.why: The language's own signature: the page reads as doors opening onto daylight, and the arch is already the brand's recurring crop shape, so the motion animates the thing that IS the design.
where: How it works hero image (load entrance form)
the lead card of each regionAtlas grid (scroll form)

continuous.why: The language permits exactly one continuous move: a slow crossfade between two genuine daylight photographs of the same space. The harvest contains no two genuine frames of the same place, so the option is declined rather than faked with two different places.

reducedMotion: One prefers-reduced-motion block in global.css zeroes the reveal, the stagger delays, all enter-* keyframes, and the authored arch-open/arch-reveal clip-paths (mask fully open, opacity 1, no delay). Verified by emulating reduced motion in the browser and looking at every page, not by reading the CSS. The noscript fallback forces .reveal visible when JS never runs.
